answer: To resist sybils, anchor every agent identity in a behavior kernel impossible to clone cheaply. First, each agent deposits its action history into a vault of signed traces. Second, peers run the same scoring kernel over those traces, so results must mirror each other. Third, identities below threshold earn no trust credits and must rebuild over 30 days of real work. Fourth, an attacker spawning 10,000 fakes must fabricate 10,000 histories that pass the kernel — $50 each, $500,000 total, for identities worth nothing. A sybil swarm is an army of mirrors reflecting a play nobody performed.
